players.product: SWEP brazed-plate heat exchangers for coolant distribution unit and chiller OEMs, plus liquid-cooling connectors and OPW couplers / cryogenic cooling infrastructure for data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 results (CEO Richard J. Tobin, CFO Chris Woenker): organic growth accelerated to 7%, led by the secular growth markets; adjusted EPS was $2.88 per share, up 10%. Third-quarter free cash flow was $383 million or 17% of revenue; year-to-date free cash flow was $703 million or 11% of revenue, up $72 million over the prior year on higher operating cash conversion, more than offsetting working-capital investment to support accelerating top-line growth.
quarterly_data.figure: organic growth 7%; adjusted EPS $2.88 (+10%); Q3 free cash flow $383 million (17% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance narrowed towards the upper end of the range (CEO Richard J. Tobin): organic growth of 5%-6% and adjusted EPS of $10.60-$10.75 per share, double-digit growth consistent with the long-term algorithm. Full-year CapEx guidance was taken up to $200 million-$220 million to reflect organic investments behind demand strength; full-year free cash flow guidance remains on track at 14%-16% of revenue (CFO Chris Woenker), with Q4 historically the highest cash-generating quarter. On the slower Q4 midpoint, the CEO said 'there's nothing based on the trajectory that we see that's any slowing. It's pure calendarization', with December customer call-offs always uncertain. Carryover restructuring benefits from footprint actions (vehicle services, polymer processing synergies, completed food retail consolidation) will be quantified with full-year guidance in January. Heading into 2027 the CEO expects carry-over restructuring savings, contributions from completed acquisitions, a lower share count and a roll-off of food retail transition costs.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 organic growth 5%-6%; adjusted EPS $10.60-$10.75; CapEx $200 million-$220 million; free cash flow 14%-16% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and backlog (CEO Richard J. Tobin): Q3 orders were up 16% year over year with growth in all five segments and a book-to-bill of 1.03. Trailing 12-month bookings are up 16%, ahead of revenue growth of 8%, with trailing book-to-bill at 1.08 and every segment growing bookings faster than revenue. Backlog is up 35% versus a year ago and up sequentially from Q2, with roughly half scheduled to ship in 2027. The CEO said the backlog is driven by where Dover has been capacity constrained - 'customers are basically getting in line to reserve that capacity'; asked about Climate & Sustainability Technologies orders, he said the backlog is 'dominated by CO2 systems demand and SWEP'; the long-cycle MAAG and Belvac businesses are 'pretty much' at a bottom and are upside to backlog build into 2027, while the short-cycle businesses have little visibility into next year.
quarterly_data.figure: orders +16% YoY; book-to-bill 1.03; trailing book-to-bill 1.08; backlog +35% YoY, roughly half shipping in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Heat exchangers and data-center liquid cooling (CEO Richard J. Tobin): shipments and order rates in brazed plate heat exchangers remain robust across all geographies and major end markets, with notable strength in liquid cooling for data centers, initially concentrated in the U.S. but now with 'meaningful acceleration in Europe and Asia'. Lead times remain extended and Dover is 'actively investing to double our global capacity for large heat exchangers through 2027'; it has been capacity constrained all year, with capacity coming on sequentially and 'a pretty big jump this quarter going into Q1', while orders keep arriving ahead of the capacity build (lead times 'not in years'). Copper exposure in SWEP is 'built into the pricing mechanism with our supplier contracts'. The CEO said Dover is not losing share on lead times, since it competes in very concentrated markets where 'those who bring on the capacity proactively tend to win'.
quarterly_data.figure: doubling global capacity for large heat exchangers through 2027

quarterly_data.signal: SWEP data-center outlook and economics (CEO Richard J. Tobin): Dover is 'ramping to double capacity' in the SWEP product line going into data centers; the CEO expects 'a shift between the central cooling system demand, which we see it now, into more CDU mix into the future'. Heat exchanger margins were robust as volumes outran the capacity investment; with direct labor less than 10% of its cost basis the business converts incremental volume exceptionally well, and a good portion of Q1 2027 revenue is already in backlog. On competition: 'Everybody wants to be in data centers'; the process is highly automated, capacity decisions are made 18 months in advance, the market is very concentrated and competitors are also announcing capacity expansion, but Dover invested in capacity ahead of the market 'so we'll get our fair share here', and 'I don't think we're getting over our skis just because our backlog says what it is'.
quarterly_data.figure: direct labor less than 10% of cost basis; capacity decisions 18 months in advance

quarterly_data.signal: Climate & Sustainability Technologies accelerated to 18% organic growth in Q3 with an 18% segment margin. CO2 systems posted record quarterly revenue, with September the highest output of the year. In refrigerated door cases, the added investment at the Richmond, Virginia facility is ramping, with line rates exiting Q3 15% higher than Q2 and another sequential increase expected in Q4; consolidation of door frame production in Sylmar, California was completed at the end of the quarter. Heat exchanger gains were offset by the cost of ramping CO2 systems, specialty cases and refrigerated door cases ahead of higher 2027 demand. Food retail has absorbed roughly $40 million of costs year to date (extra labor for the ramp and duplicate fixed costs of two facilities), a number the CEO said will probably go up by year end before productivity flips; he expects those costs to progressively get better and 'probably finish up by the end of Q1', does not expect them to flow through in total into 2027 unless volume drops, and sees 'no indication of volume dropping in 2027' based on the backlog. He expects segment margins 'to improve meaningfully in 2027', said Dover is 'well on track' for its segment targets and 'we will beat our comp in Q1'.
quarterly_data.figure: CST organic growth 18%; segment margin 18%; door-case line rates +15% vs Q2; ~$40 million food retail ramp costs year to date

quarterly_data.signal: Secular growth markets (CEO Richard J. Tobin) now represent over 25% of total revenue, up from 18% in 2024, and are a material driver of 2026 revenue growth, a trend expected to continue in 2027. Dover added capacity in advance of the market to capture leadership positions, particularly in energy transition and power generation, CO2 systems, data centers and cryogenic components serving the energy and space markets; the vast majority of acquisition capital over the past five years went into these markets, which remain the top organic and inorganic priorities. Customers across the broader portfolio are 'beginning to order into 2027', earlier than in a normal year.
quarterly_data.figure: secular growth markets over 25% of revenue (18% in 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: Organic capacity program (CEO Richard J. Tobin, slide nine): greenfield expansions are under way in below-ground retail fueling, cryogenic components, flow meters in the U.S. and single-use biopharma components in Asia, plus capacity investments in printer ink production and specialty cases in CO2 systems and large heat exchangers; many projects will be online by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Greenfield sites are sized for multi-year demand; the CEO hopes for additional capacity expansion beyond what is announced, which would mean more demand than the initial sizing. Organic investment remains Dover's highest-return use of capital.
quarterly_data.figure: many projects online by end of Q1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments in Q3 (CEO Richard J. Tobin): Engineered Products was down 2% organically, with strong aerospace and defense component demand more than offset by lower European vehicle services volumes; margin stable. Imaging & Identification grew 2% organically, led by double-digit growth in serialization software, with margins up 400 basis points to 33% (the CEO called the year-to-date margin 'entirely sustainable'; a new plant in Poland was built this year and ink production rebuilding finishes in 2027). Pumps & Process Solutions grew 1% organically, with growth in AI and energy infrastructure, single-use biopharma and industrial pumps partly offset by lower polymer processing equipment volumes (quoting activity high); margin expanded 770 basis points to 34% on industrial pumps, precision components and a higher biopharma mix.
quarterly_data.figure: Engineered Products down 2% organic; Imaging & Identification +2%, margin 33% (+400 bps); Pumps & Process Solutions +1%, margin 34% (+770 bps)

quarterly_data.signal: Clean Energy & Fueling grew 12% organically with solid shipments and orders in clean energy components, fluid transport and North American retail fueling, which posted its strongest quarter in years; margin was roughly flat as volume leverage was offset by the cryogenic production ramp. CEO Richard J. Tobin: earnings spreads on fueling products have been up substantially over the past 18 to 24 months and he does not expect that to narrow; supply constraints on underground tank equipment (which Dover does not supply) are lengthening the demand cycle - called a three-year capex cycle a year and a half ago, 'we could probably argue that it's going to be at least four'; Dover is expanding in the products around the tanks, where demand is robust and margins are quite good. Asked where the platform stands on the 25% margin Dover had talked about, the CEO said 'Look, we're tracking there.'
quarterly_data.figure: Clean Energy & Fueling organic growth 12%; fueling capex cycle at least four years

quarterly_data.signal: Bolt-on acquisitions announced in the quarter (CEO Richard J. Tobin): Cloeren, closed in August, adds extrusion dies and feed blocks to the MAAG polymer processing platform and more than 300,000 sq ft of U.S. manufacturing capacity close to the U.S. petrochemical and space launch infrastructure; Leistung, signed and expected to close in the fourth quarter, gives Clean Energy & Fueling a low-cost cryogenics components manufacturing presence in India. Both carry excess capacity that other Dover operating companies will use as manufacturing hubs. The CEO said M&A activity naturally slows in Q4, Dover lost some assets that sold above its return criteria, the pipeline still holds 'some interesting stuff', and organic investment is 'probably going to drive as much revenue growth as kind of bolt-on acquisitions would do'.
quarterly_data.figure: Cloeren: more than 300,000 sq ft of U.S. manufacturing capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing (CEO Richard J. Tobin): Dover moved up pricing decisions this year and accelerated price introductions in certain instances depending on exposure to commodity group metals and other inputs, rather than waiting for the start of the year: 'I think we're actually probably a full quarter in front of getting in front of that' on price-cost into 2027. Asked whether higher interest rates affect its capital-planning businesses, the CEO said: 'None.'

players.product: Microwave Products Group RF filters, amplifiers and switches for satellites; cryogenic vacuum-jacketed piping and valves for launch infrastructure

quarterly_data.signal: Space-related capacity (CEO Richard J. Tobin): demand for Dover's cryogenic components in LNG and space launch infrastructure 'remains healthy, with several recent high-profile project wins'; where demand runs ahead of capacity Dover is expanding, with additional output coming online in the first quarter of 2027. Dover is also making capacity investments in radio frequency equipment for space. The CEO said the cryogenic opportunities found over the past 18 months are driving the top line but require heavy investment, slightly dilutive to margins during the build phase.
quarterly_data.figure: additional cryogenic output online in Q1 2027
